problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate budget across 11 infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are:  
* Project Alpha: benefit score 0.070, environmental impact 0.245, allocation range [0.099, 0.695]  
* Project Beta: benefit score 0.079, environmental impact 0.127, allocation range [0.082, 0.635]  
* Project Gamma: benefit score 0.070, environmental impact 0.103, allocation range [0.034, 0.476]  
* Project Delta: benefit score 0.138, environmental impact 0.051, allocation range [0.071, 0.582]  
* Project Epsilon: benefit score 0.191, environmental impact 0.017, allocation range [0.069, 0.745]  
* Project Zeta: benefit score 0.137, environmental impact 0.154, allocation range [0.064, 0.735]  
* Project Eta: benefit score 0.054, environmental impact 0.096, allocation range [0.048, 0.635]  
* Project Theta: benefit score 0.113, environmental impact 0.273, allocation range [0.094, 0.848]  
* Project Iota: benefit score 0.063, environmental impact 0.127, allocation range [0.036, 0.868]  
* Project Kappa: benefit score 0.030, environmental impact 0.224, allocation range [0.030, 0.840]  
* Project Lambda: benefit score 0.174, environmental impact 0.179, allocation range [0.017, 0.693]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified range, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to 1. To ensure equitable service coverage, the group of high-priority projects L = {Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Epsilon, Zeta, Theta, Iota, Kappa, Lambda} must collectively receive at least 0.596 of the total budget. Additionally, the total environmental impact index of the portfolio must not exceed 0.211, and the overall community benefit score must be at least 0.071. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
